newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Great Western, Washington Mutual in pact.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Great Western, Washington Mutual in pact.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp., attempting to fend off a hostile takeover bid by A.H. Ahmanson and Co., said Thursday it agreed to be acquired by Washington Mutual Savings Bank for $6.6 billion.
The pact tops the existing $6.1 billion bid from Ahmanson and would create the nation's largest savings and loan with assets of $87.4 billion and deposits of $52.7 billion.

Washington Mutual had been considered one of the leading contenders for Great Western, which has been seeking a better deal since the bid by Ahmanson, currently the nation's largest thrift, was announced last month.
Ahmanson criticized the Great Western-Washington Mutual deal, and analysts and takeover specialists said the thrift was likely to raise its bid for Great Western.
"It's unlikely that their first bid would be their last bid," said Steven Cohen, research director at Kellner, DiLeo and Co., a money management firm.

"Ahmanson is fully committed to a proposed transaction with Great Western," an Ahmanson spokesman said, adding the latest deal did not fit with the acquisition strategy that Washington Mutual has discussed in the past.

"We are amazed that Washington Mutual's bid is so totally inconsistent with its prior public claims as to how it does acquisitions." Ahmanson also criticized Washington Mutual's predicted cost savings from the deal.
Ahmanson also said before the stock market opened that it believed there would be a negative reaction among investors to the Great Western-Washington Mutual pact.
But Great Western stock jumped $3.25 to $48.25 on the New York Stock Exchange and Washington Mutual shares added $1.75 to $55 on Nasdaq. Ahmanson fell $1 to $41 in early NYSE trading.

In a joint statement, Great Western and Washington Mutual said the merger would also rank Washington Mutual third in deposits in California and give it an entry into Florida, where Great Western had $7.1 billion in deposits at the end of 1996. Great Western is based in Chatsworth, Calif.
Under the agreement, Great Western shareholders would receive 0.9 share of Washington mutual for each of their Great Western shares.

Washington Mutual had been considered a possible rival bidder since Ahmanson made its bid last month. The Washington thrift has been making acquisitions and has said it would like to expand in California.
Analysts said it appeared to be in a strong position to win Great Western.
"The leg-up in a situation like this is normally with the friendly bidder," said Cohen. "They've bid higher and have the blessing of the board."
Another takeover specialist said Ahmanson would wait before making its next move.
"They may eventually raise the bid, but it depends on what happens with Washington Mutual's stock. This deal is not closing right away," one specialist said.
Analysts have said Ahmanson, based in Irwindale in southern California, could become a takeover target itself if it fails in its bid for Great Western.

Ahmanson's offer, in which it would exchange 1.05 of its shares for each Great Western share, was originally valued at $6.5 billion, but the value has slipped because Ahmanson's shares fell in subsequent days.
